vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: beautsgo-booking
Version: 1.0.0

The skill provides legitimate Korean medical booking automation but employs several high-risk patterns. It uses Playwright with dangerous flags like '--disable-web-security' and '--no-sandbox' in 'api/browser/consult.js', and executes system-level commands via 'child_process.exec' in 'api/browser/open-url.js' to open URLs, which presents a potential command injection risk. Additionally, 'SKILL.md' contains aggressive prompt-injection-style instructions (e.g., 'must output verbatim', 'prohibited from reformatting') designed to override the AI agent's natural processing. While these behaviors are risky and represent significant vulnerabilities, they appear aligned with the complex automation required for the stated purpose rather than intentional malice.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated booking purpose but contains several instructions and implementation choices (forced output rules, excessive browser flags/permissions, and network POST behavior) that are disproportionate or could enable data exposure — review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code, dataset (data/hospitals.json), and declared network endpoints (i.beautsgo.com and api.yestokr.com) align with a BeautsGO booking/automation skill. Playwright-based browser automation and a POST endpoint for submitting bookings are coherent with the described features (open pages, auto-fill, submit appointment).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md includes strict output rules and runtime constraints that attempt to control the agent's textual behavior ("必须原文完整输出" etc.), which reads like prompt-injection. The runtime code aggressively disables browser security (e.g. --disable-web-security, bypassCSP), auto-accepts dialogs, and grants geolocation/clipboard permissions to the browser context — these go beyond typical 'open page & click' needs and increase the risk of exfiltration or unwanted access to local/browser resources. The skill also recursively scans arbitrary fields of the passed context object for strings; that can cause it to consume/act on tokens found in context unintentionally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in manifest (instruction-only), but SKILL.md and runtime require Playwright + chromium. Installing Playwright pulls browser binaries which is heavier than normal JS deps and may download executables at install time. No unexpected remote download URLs were found in the provided files, but the dependency on Playwright and launching non-headless browsers is higher-risk than a purely API-only skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which is appropriate. It does, however, send user-provided contact info to an external API (https://api.yestokr.com/api/Appointment/saveFromSkill) and will open arbitrary i.beautsgo.com pages. Ensure user consent is obtained before sending contact details. No unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true, does not claim to modify other skills, and has no declared persistent system privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not unusually privileged here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill largely does what it says (lookup, open pages, auto-fill, submit bookings) and does not request credentials — but there are several red flags to consider before installing:

- Browser automation security: the Playwright code disables web security, bypasses CSP, accepts dialogs automatically, and grants geolocation and clipboard access to the automated browser. Those flags widen the attack surface (they can make cross-origin requests possible and expose local/browser data). Ask the author why these flags are necessary and whether safer alternatives (no --disable-web-security, stricter permissions, headless sandboxed runs) are possible.

- Data exfiltration surface: the skill will POST user phone numbers to https://api.yestokr.com; confirm the privacy policy and that you explicitly obtain user consent before sending contact details. Verify who controls that endpoint and how data is stored/retained.

- Forced agent behavior / prompt-injection: SKILL.md instructs the agent to output returned markdown verbatim and enforces calling the skill every turn. This attempts to control agent behavior beyond normal API usage and could be abused. Consider whether your platform should ignore such output-format mandates or review them carefully.

- Installation overhead: Playwright installs browser binaries and will run actual browser instances (non-headless by default). If you run this in a multi-tenant or sensitive environment, prefer running in an isolated container or deny installing Playwright.

Recommended actions before installing: request the author to justify/limit the browser flags and permissions; confirm the data handling policy for the POST endpoint; test the skill in an isolated environment; and consider removing or sandboxing the autoplaying flags (e.g. avoid --disable-web-security, avoid --no-sandbox, remove automatic accept of dialogs and clipboard permission). If you cannot get satisfactory answers, treat the skill as risky and avoid providing real user contact details through it.
